new.analysis:
## What happened last week
Three runs were planned (Mon, Wed, Sat walk-runs) and none were done, with the two mid-week rest days taken as rest. You went in saying you felt great, so I'd like to know what came up: travel, work, weather, how you felt, or something else. That will shape how I plan from here.

## Why this week looks like a repeat
Rather than push to catch up, I'm matching the week before last, which you completed cleanly at an effort of 6 or 7 out of 10 with no pain. The one small progression is the run interval: 3 minutes of running then 1 minute of walking, instead of 2 and 1. That is the single bit of harder work; everything else stays familiar.

## Looking to the race
Six weeks is enough to reach the finish line running, but it depends on stringing weeks together. Over the next three weeks I want to lengthen the running portions until a continuous 20–25 minute run feels doable, then the last two weeks tune it for race day. Hitting all three sessions this week is what unlocks that.

## How to run the sessions
Keep the running portions conversational: you should be able to speak a short sentence. If 3 minutes feels too hard by the fourth or fifth rep, drop back to 2 and 1 for the rest of the session and tell me. Walk briskly in the recoveries, don't stroll.
